items.title: Google's March 2026 Core Update: Clicks Collapsing Despite Stable Rankings
items.summary: Google's March 2026 core update has resulted in stable rankings and even increased impressions for many sites, but clicks are plummeting due to AI Overviews providing answers directly in search results. Analysis across 12 B2B SaaS sites reveals up to 58% CTR drops for informational content like explainers and how-tos. Experts recommend auditing CTR, pivoting to transactional content, and incorporating unique data to combat interception.

items.title: Google's March 2026 Update and Surging AI Overviews Demand Agency Action Plan
items.summary: The March 2026 Google update has impacted rankings from below while AI Overviews for shopping queries increased 5.6x to 14%, severely affecting CTR. Emarketed provides a comprehensive guide for SEO agencies to adapt. Focuses on strategies to navigate dual threats of core updates and AI search changes.

items.title: Google's March 2026 Core Update Powered by Gemini 4.0 Targets AI Slop
items.summary: Google's March 2026 Core Update, driven by Gemini 4.0, filters out low-value AI-generated content lacking 'Zero Information Gain.' It prioritizes deep, original, human-quality content for better rankings. This marks a stronger push against AI slop in search results.

items.title: Digital Marketing News March 11-20, 2026: Google Core Update Hits 55% of Sites
items.summary: Google's March core update impacted 55% of monitored sites, emphasizing information gain, AI content detection via Gemini 4.0, and stricter E-E-A-T for YMYL topics. Additional news includes ChatGPT ads at $60 CPM and AI Mode reaching 75M daily users. Provides actionable insights for digital marketers.

items.title: Horror Novel 'Shy Girl' Canceled Over Suspected A.I. Use
items.summary: Hachette Book Group canceled the U.S. release of Mia Ballard's horror novel 'Shy Girl' following allegations that AI was used to assist in writing it, despite the author's contractual attestation of sole authorship. The controversy has ignited discussions on AI detection tools and the absence of standardized policies among publishers regarding AI-generated content. Publishers maintain a firm stance against AI but lack effective preventive measures.

items.title: Why an AI firm known for fighting plagiarism has real authors in a fury
items.summary: Grammarly, an AI writing tool, has drawn ire from authors by attributing AI-generated expert writing advice to real authors' names. The incident underscores ethical concerns in AI applications for writing and editing assistance. It highlights tensions between AI tools and traditional authorship integrity.

items.title: Book Deals: Week of March 23, 2026
items.summary: Publishers Weekly reports recent major deals including Berkley acquiring two adult debut novels from YA author Karen M. McManus in a significant two-book contract. Montlake secured Sara Field's lupine romance series among other notable acquisitions. These deals reflect ongoing activity in the publishing industry for genre fiction.

items.title: Publishers Maintain Firm Line Against AI But Lack Clear Policies
items.summary: Authors Guild President W. Ralph Eubanks highlights how publishers require authors to attest no AI use in contracts but have few measures to enforce it, citing the New York Times article on the 'Shy Girl' cancellation. The post underscores vulnerabilities in current publishing practices amid rising AI concerns.

items.title: Grammarly AI Scandal Angers Real Authors
items.summary: Pulitzer-winning columnist Michael Hiltzik shares a Los Angeles Times article exposing Grammarly for using real authors' names on AI-generated content. The post amplifies authors' fury over the misuse of their identities in AI writing advice.

items.title: Woke Gatekeepers Try to Ban Conservative Novel 'Life in Woke America'
items.summary: Author Joel Rakow details how 'woke gatekeepers' and the 'censorship cartel' attempted to suppress his novel through threats and blacklisting before publication. He shares his article 'Writing a Conservative Novel in Woke America' and rallies support against erasure of conservative storytelling. The post questions future free speech battles in publishing.

items.summary: Fans express frustration with excessive woke elements in Hollywood productions, particularly the latest season of 'The Boys,' which many abandoned after one or two episodes. items.title: DEI Backlash to Michael B. Jordan's 2026 Oscar Win
items.summary: Critics accuse the Academy of awarding Michael B. Jordan Best Actor for DEI reasons rather than merit, drawing parallels to Sidney Poitier's historic win. They claim the obscure film and Jordan's performance did not justify the honor. This illustrates audience skepticism toward diversity-driven awards.

items.title: 10 Ways Small Businesses Are Using AI Right Now That Large Corporations Haven’t Figured Out Yet
items.summary: Small businesses are outpacing large corporations by using AI for tasks like 24/7 phone answering, cash flow forecasting, bias-free hiring, and personalized marketing without needing big teams or permissions. Tools enable operations to run autonomously, competitor spying, and automations, leading to revenue boosts for 91% of users. 68% of small businesses now use AI daily, resulting in more hiring.

items.title: OpenClaw's Paperclip: Build a Full AI Company on Your Own Computer
items.summary: OpenClaw's new Paperclip plugin allows small business owners to create autonomous AI teams including CEO, marketing, and tech roles with persistent memory that work daily without management or salaries. It runs locally on your hardware for data privacy. Users can download from GitHub and start with one task to replace operations teams.

items.title: Durable Launches End-to-End AI Business Platform for Entrepreneurs
items.summary: Durable has launched an updated end-to-end AI platform designed specifically for small business owners and entrepreneurs, extending beyond website creation to full business operations. The platform aims to make starting and running a small business straightforward and default choice. This move democratizes business tools with AI automation.

items.title: Denovo Unveils AI Launchpad to Democratize Entrepreneurship
items.summary: On March 18, 2026, Denovo introduced its AI Launchpad, a new toolset to lower barriers for aspiring entrepreneurs and small businesses using AI-powered features. The platform accelerates business startup and operations. It targets widespread adoption amid rising AI use in SMBs.
